title: When compiling with `deprecated=no` on the `master` branch, more errors appear when testing
body:
### Tested versions

master [51105ccbe58381774ecd7a7486d564b202a5192e] with `deprecated=no`
Not reproducible on master [51105ccbe58381774ecd7a7486d564b202a5192e] with `deprecated=yes` (default)
(Can't say if this is a regression because it's based on deprecated stuff)

### System information

Godot v4.8.dev (51105ccbe) - macOS Sequoia (15.7.5) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Metal (Forward+) - integrated Apple M4 (Apple9) - Apple M4 (10 threads) - 16.00 GiB memory - CoreAudio (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

These errors don't appear when `deprecated=yes` (the default).

- [ ] `Color8` is obvious to me (it was deprecated in #100825), so I think it should be replaced with `Color.from_rgba8`. Edit: I learned about #105686. This means the `const` test can't use `Color.from_rgba8` until this is fixed.

- [ ] I also know about `PackedDataContainer` (it was deprecated in #105990). I don't think it's really needed in this test, so it can be removed. Edit: @HolonProduction suggested in RocketChat that it could be replaced with a test-only class of the same functionality. Personally, it seems kind of out of place, especially since the below issue is there, but considering #121921, it makes sense to have test-only classes for some stuff, to have to prevent updating them every time something gets deprecated. #122485 for reference.

- [ ] As for the `modules/gdscript/tests/scripts/runtime/errors/compat_get_property_list.gd` errors, from the filename, it seems like it's a backwards compatibility test, so it's probably meant to check the deprecated stuff. In that case, idk how to disable it for `deprecated=no`, then. Maybe by putting it in a separate folder called `deprecated` and editing the runner to exclude those on `deprecated=no`. Edit: This was added in #119210 to fix #118877. I don't really know why the test was necessary since I haven't seen any other test used to specifically test compatibility, but since it's there, it can be a precedent for more deprecated-only tests, which would require changes to the runner.

- [x] I don't know why `modules/gdscript/tests/test_completion.h:211` isn't empty when deprecated or what the purpose of this is. It's not clear what's causing it. Edit: I figured it out and made a PR for it. #122634 for reference

- [ ] The `SplitContainer` errors mostly seem to be relating to the child's width and height being 2px less than expected. But I don't know off my top of my head why that's somehow impacted by deprecated stuff. Edit: It was #90411 that added the `DISABLE_DEPRECATED` `#ifdef`. Since only  the `[SceneTree][SplitContainer] Two children` test case fails, it makes sense. I'm not exactly sure what the code in the `DISABLE_DEPRECATED` `#ifdef` does to make the tests work that nothing else can, and if that's desired in the future (since it can support multiple children now), and if it needs to be deprecated.

### Steps to reproduce

- Compile `master` with the below build command.
- Run `doctest` by suffixing with `--test` in command-line
- Notice the errors

This was the build command:
`scons platform=macos dev_build=true module_visual_shader_enabled=yes deprecated=no tests=yes`

Ofc, change out `macos` with your platform, and add any other commands you usually use to build your binary. (I don't think `module_visual_shader_enabled=yes` is needed for this either but JIC)

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

See #121921, but TLDR: Not safe/beneficial/compatible to upload binaries.
